name: Hyunsoo Cha

papers.title: Robot-Factored World Models via Robot Rendering
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned video world models predict future observations from an initial observation and an action signal. In robotics, this action signal becomes future video in two stages: a robot body and controller realize it as motion, and the scene responds through contact, occlusion, and object motion. Conditioning directly on the pre-realization signal asks the video model to learn robot-specific controller semantics, while conditioning on logged future states leaks interaction outcomes. We propose robot-factored world models, which target the middle signal: a deployment-available nominal trajectory produced by the robot's own controller and kinematics before observing scene interaction. Together with camera-aware static RGB/depth context, this rendered nominal geometry forms a shared visual world-model interface for fixed and dynamic viewpoints. The video model sees the action only as visible nominal geometry, and learns how objects, surfaces, and occlusions change around it. On DROID and RoboCasa-GR1, this rendered interface improves over Cartesian/vector action-conditioning baselines, while motion-source and depth ablations isolate the value of nominalization and 3D contact cues. We further probe the same rendered-prompt interface through counterfactual trajectory redirection, held-out embodiment composition, and human demonstration to robot video.
